quotes.text: A few of the reviews here have drawn comparisons to Madonna, and well yeah. Je t'aime mélancolie especially compares with Vogue's housey piano sound, but I'd speculate that Boutonnat (Farmer's composer and producer) had at least some exposure to the likes of Grace Jones before putting this album together. L'autre also has the theatricality of Trevor Horn, and I'm here for it.

The sultry tones of John Malkovich and John Hurt aside, there's some pretty solid synthpop here. Kinda Pet Shop Boys in parts, a little Madonna in others. The crow actually reflects a slight gothic tinge in the music, as heard in "Agnus Dei" and "Beyond My Control".
my ears love this dark, romantic, art pop stuff

This one showed an evolution of the singer : indeed, the texts marked a change of mindset and testified to a transformation in her life including a greater openness to the other (hence the album's title). From that moment, the singer decided to more express herself and went to the meeting of her fellow man.
Writing for five months, this album was the result of all what has happened to Farmer "at personal and artistic levels".

Laurent Boutonnat decided to record the songs of the album in English-language, but they were ultimately not used. He also wanted to release as singles all the songs from the album, but that didn't happen because of a lack of money.

DeBaser rated the album three stars out of five and observed that while effective, the album's sound is very simple, little refined , suggesting that it was not as musically ambitious as her later work.
